name: Darwin Initiative Capability & Capacity

funder.name: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra)

summary: UK government grants of £75,000 to £250,000 for one- to three-year projects that build the skills and capacity of local and national organisations to deliver biodiversity conservation and poverty reduction.

geography.label: Darwin Initiative Round 32 eligible countries (within listed biodiversity hotspots)

reporting: Annual and half-year progress reports, reviewed each year, against the project's objectives (outputs, ethics, environmental impact), plus a final report at the end of the award.

steps: Initial review, expert assessment and sift meeting

eligibility.rule: Work in both an eligible country and an eligible hotspot or marine/freshwater environment
Not a foreign government or agency, except a qualifying government-funded university
Have a local or national organisation lead or partner in each project country and engage stakeholders early
Keep annual requested funds within 25% of average annual turnover or income over 3 years
Promote economic development and welfare in eligible countries as a primary objective
Lead no more than one application per scheme in Round 32
Focuses on building the capability and capacity of identified local and national organisations

documents: Signed cover letter on the lead organisation’s letterhead
Two sets of audited or independently examined accounts, or other evidence of financial capacity
CVs or job descriptions of key project staff
Letters of support from all project partners

opens.quote: The latest application round opened on Friday 22nd May 2026.

administered_by.quote: NIRAS Darwin Initiative Administrator; first point of contact for projects and applicants.

geography.quote: In Round 32, parts of 36 countries are eligible.

access.quote: All applications should be submitted via the Flexi-Grant application portal.

window.quote: Applications to Darwin Initiative Capability & Capacity are a single-stage process.

amount.quote: Darwin Initiative Capability & Capacity welcomes applications for projects between £75,000 and £250,000.

reporting.quote: Projects must provide Annual and Half Year progress reports that are reviewed each year.

effort.quote: Applications to Darwin Initiative Capability & Capacity are a single-stage process. Deadline for applications: Monday 31st August 2026.
1) Initial Review: Applications that are poor quality, incomplete or do not meet the essential eligibility criteria or standard will be rejected.
3) Sift meeting: The experts discuss comments and agree the strongest applications to recommend for funding or inviting to Stage 2 (repeating step 2 and 3).

eligibility.quote: Projects must work within both an eligible country and an eligible hotspot (or marine/freshwater environment).

Foreign governments and their agencies cannot be Lead Organisations, except for universities that receive government funding (providing the application they are submitting isn't for "business as usual" work that should be covered by the government funding, as per the usual requirements).
Russian organisations are ineligible to be a Lead Organisation or Partner or involved in any way with any Biodiversity Challenge Fund grant.
All projects are required to be led by or partner with local/national organisations of the country/ies in which it is based, with the meaningful and early engagement of incountry stakeholders.
The maximum annual value of funds requested should not exceed 25% of the Lead Organisation's average annual turnover/income for the previous 3 years.

Darwin Initiative is entirely Official Development Assistance (ODA) funded, and therefore projects must promote the economic development and welfare of eligible countries (see Annex A) as a primary objective.
Under Round 32, organisations can only lead one application per scheme.
Projects must focus on developing the capability and capacity of identified local and national organisations

after_award.quote: Projects must provide Annual and Half Year progress reports that are reviewed each year. These reports must provide robust reporting against intended objectives and include information on outputs, ethics and environmental impact. All projects are required to submit a Final Report at the end of the award.

Projects over £50k but under £100k need an audit statement which can be by an independent examiner and need not be a formal audit. Projects over £100k but under £1,000,000 need an end of project audit.

documents.quote: The budget spreadsheet for Darwin Initiative Capability & Capacity projects can be found below.
It should be presented on the lead organisation’s letterhead and appropriately signed.
Two sets of audited or independently examined accounts covering the last three financial years
Safeguarding Policy and other associated polices (see 2.6) must be submitted as a single PDF file.
1 side of A4 per CVs in English (or job descriptions if vacant) of all the key project staff named in the application form
Required from all project partners (including from the lead organisation) on headed paper
